ayahOccurrences.text: وَجَعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ ٱلْحَرْثِ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ نَصِيبًا فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَهَٰذَا لِشُرَكَآئِنَا ۖ فَمَا كَانَ لِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ فَلَا يَصِلُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ فَهُوَ يَصِلُ إِلَىٰ شُرَكَآئِهِمْ ۗ سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ

ayahOccurrences.text: وَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَنْعَٰمٌ وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ لَّا يَطْعَمُهَآ إِلَّا مَن نَّشَآءُ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَأَنْعَٰمٌ حُرِّمَتْ ظُهُورُهَا وَأَنْعَٰمٌ لَّا يَذْكُرُونَ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا ٱفْتِرَآءً عَلَيْهِ ۚ سَيَجْزِيهِم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْتَرُونَ

; bounty, blessings, grace, good living, to enjoy life, to bestow favours; to flourish, to become verdant; to be soft and smooth.

lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
أَنْعَمَ ʾanʿama [v. IV trans.]

1 to bestow (a favour), to grant (a blessing)

(8:53) ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَكُ مُغَيِّرًا نِعْمَةً أَنْعَمَهَا عَلَى قَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ that is because God would never change a favour He had conferred on a people until they [first] changed that which is within themselves

2 [with prep. عَلَى] to bless

(1:7) صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ the path of those You have blessed.

entries.label: نَاعِمَةٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَاعِمَةٌ nāʿimatun [fem. act. part.] radiant, serene

(88:8) وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ some faces on that Day will be radiant.

entries.label: نَعَمٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَعَمٌ naʿam (1) [coll. n., pl. أَنْعَامٌ ʾanʿām] cattle, livestock, domestic animals

(5:95) وَمَنْ قَتَلَهُ مِنْكُمْ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاءٌ مِثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ whoever of you kills it intentionally, the compensation is the equivalent of whatever livestock he has killed; * الأنعام name of Sura 6, Meccan sura, so‐named because of the reference in verses 136–

47 to the ‘Livestock’.

entries.label: نَعَمْ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَعَمْ naʿam (2) [exclamation, affirm. particle of response] yes, yes indeed

(7:44) فَهَلْ وَجَدْتُمْ مَا وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ حَقًّا قَالُوا نَعَمْ ‘so, have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?’–they will answer, ‘Yes.’

entries.label: نَعِيمٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَعِيمٌ naʿım [n.] bliss, grace, delight, happiness

(52:17) أِنَّ المُتّّقِينَ فِى جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ those who were mindful of God are in Gardens and bliss; *

(70:38) جَنَّاتُ النَّعِيم Paradise [lit. Gardens of Bliss].

entries.label: نَعَّمَ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَعَّمَ naʿʿama [v. II trans.] to grant good living or a life of ease, to bless with comfort in this world

(89:15) فَأَمَّا الإِنْسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلاَهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ as for man, whenever his Lord, testing him, honours him and grants him ease of living.

entries.label: نَعْمَاءُ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَعْمَاءُ naʿmāʾ [n.] grace, favour, ease of living

(11:10) وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ نَعْمَاءَ بَعْدَ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ and if We let him taste ease and plenty after a hardship that touched him.

entries.label: نَعْمَةٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَعْمَةٌ naʿmatun [n.] pleasure, joy, good living, affluence

(73:11) وَذَرْنِى وَالمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِى النَّعْمِةِ and leave Me [to deal] with the deniers, the rich in the pleasures of good living.

entries.label: نِعِمَّا
entries.definitionHtml:
نِعِمَّا niʿimmā [compound unit of v. نِعْمَ niʿma + relat. مَا] ‘how praiseworthy!’

(2:271) إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ if you openly give charity, how praiseworthy it is …!

entries.label: نِعْمَ
entries.definitionHtml:
نِعْمَ niʿma [defective v. of praise followed by a def. n. as subject] ‘what a praiseworthy …!’, ‘what a perfect …!’

(38:44) إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ We have surely found him steadfast–what an excellent servant!

entries.label: نِعْمَةٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نِعْمَةٌ niʿmatun I [n., pl. نِعَمٌ niʿam and أَنْعُم ʾanʿum] favour, bounty

(31:20) وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً and He has lavished upon you His bounties, [both] apparent and hidden II [coll. n.] favours, blessings, grace

(16:18) وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لاَ تُحْصُوهَا if you tried to count God’s blessings, you could never take them all in III [v. n./n.] the act of bestowing favours

(52:29) فَذَكِّرْ فَمَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ وَلاَ مَجْنُونٍ so [Prophet] remind [all], for you are, by your Lord’s favouring you, neither a soothsayer nor a madman.
